card.name: Danza de Tijeras
card.profile: The Danza de las tijeras (Quechua: Supaypa wasin tusuq) is a competitive ritual dance of Chanka origin from Peru’s south-central Andes. Each danzaq wields polished iron rods resembling scissors blades, forming a cuadrilla with violinist and harpist; two or more cuadrillas face off in an atipanakuy duel of step-dancing and acrobatics. Danzaq descend from tusuq laykas (pre-Hispanic priests) persecuted in the colony as "supaypa waman"; while costumed, dancers are barred from churches. UNESCO-inscribed 2010.
card.insight: UNESCO element 00391: "The competition or atipanakuy may last up to ten hours... physical ability, quality of the instruments, and expertise of the accompanying musicians, are all evaluated."
